consensus_summary: Consensus responses identify no single settled meaning but converge on a dominant cluster: barley as the humble/lowly grain or bread of the poor (via John 6 loaves, Gideon’s barley cake, Ruth gleaning, cheaper pricing) intertwined with or alternatively as the early Passover-season firstfruits grain whose wave sheaf typifies Christ’s resurrection (Lev 23, 1 Cor 15).
book_summary: Barley is the firstfruits—the first and humblest grain reaped in spring; the sheaf waved before the LORD, which is Christ risen.
consensus_core_identification: Humble/poor-man’s grain and/or Passover firstfruits typifying Christ risen
book_core_identification: Firstfruits (first and humblest spring grain) as the waved sheaf that is Christ risen
boundary_disagreement: None; both center on the same firstfruits-plus-humility cluster and leave secondary associations (scarcity pricing, jealousy offering, pure allegory of the Law) as peripheral.
rationale: Minimum cores are identical: the early humble grain whose firstfruits sheaf is Christ. Consensus already treats the two themes as intertwined or primary/alternative; the book simply states that combination in compact form. Wording and emphasis differences (e.g., presence or absence of John 6) are immaterial.
strongest_objection: Some consensus strands elevate pure socio-economic humility (John 6, Rev 6) over the firstfruits typology, and Lev 23 does not explicitly name barley, so a reader could claim the book over-specifies the Christ identification.
